sources.note: Trains a 1.5B reasoning model to emit one of three mode tokens (NoThink, Short, Long) as the very first token of its response and to reason under that mode's budget, learned end-to-end inside GRPO with no separate router.
sources.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation

sources.note: ChainPrune merges semantically equivalent steps from 16 sampled reasoning paths into a tree, picks Pareto-dominant short paths as DPO preference data, and fine-tunes with an added NLL term, cutting tokens 28.1% and reasoning steps 26.8% on two R1-distilled models without losing accuracy.
sources.title: ChainPrune: Evaluating and Reducing Redundancy in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

sources.note: The paper segments LRM reasoning traces into cognitive steps with Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, labels each step with one of Bloom's six levels, and uses the resulting level proportions and 6x6 transition matrix to profile seven reasoning models and to predict solution correctness.
sources.title: Cognitive Profiling of LRMs' Reasoning Traces Using Bloom's Taxonomy

sources.note: Ada-R1 merges a long-CoT and a short-CoT model into one hybrid, then applies two levels of preference training so the model first picks a reasoning style per problem and then prefers the shorter correct trace within that style, cutting average reasoning length by about 51% on five maths datasets.
sources.title: Ada-R1: Hybrid-CoT via Bi-Level Adaptive Reasoning Optimization

sources.note: ShorterBetter takes the length of the shortest correct response in a sampled group as a per-problem target and rewards the model for matching it, cutting output length by 50%-80% on DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B.
sources.title: ShorterBetter: Guiding Reasoning Models to Find Optimal Inference Length for Efficient Reasoning

instructions:
Revise the wiki definition for 'DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B'.

It was written against fewer sources than the archive now holds. The sources below are all of them, including the ones that have arrived since.

This is the definition as it stands:

    DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is a language model that archived papers train and evaluate on, not a concept, method or dataset; the wiki has no kind for a model, so it is filed under the least wrong of the three available. It is the smallest distilled reasoning model the archive's length-reduction work uses, and in both citing papers it appears as the small sibling of the 7B model that carries the headline numbers. Ada-R1 merges a long-CoT and a short-CoT version of it into one hybrid and applies bi-level preference training, covering AIME25, MATH500, GSM8K, OlympiadBench and Minerva Math -- though the reported 50.93% length cut at a 1.65-point accuracy cost is measured on the 7B. ShorterBetter trains it on 40K DeepScaleR-preview mathematics problems with a per-problem target set by the shortest correct sampled response, reporting a 50%-80% output-length reduction across the 1.5B/7B pair both in and out of domain; neither paper reports the model's architecture or separate capability figures beyond those runs.

If the new sources change nothing, return it unchanged; that is a real answer and it records that somebody checked.

A definition that enumerates its sources by name is the one most likely to be quietly wrong now. Prefer stating what the term means to counting where it appears.

result.definition: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is the smallest of the DeepSeek-R1 distillations and the model the archive's length-reduction work uses when it wants a second scale alongside the 7B. It is filed as a model; earlier wiki text said the wiki had no kind for one, which is no longer true. Across the sources it plays two roles. As a training target it is the small sibling: Ada-R1 merges long-CoT and short-CoT versions of it under bi-level preference training across AIME25, MATH500, GSM8K, OlympiadBench and Minerva Math, though its headline 50.93% length cut at a 1.65-point accuracy cost is measured on the 7B; ShorterBetter trains it on 40K DeepScaleR-preview problems against a per-problem target set by the shortest correct sampled response, reporting 50%-80% output-length reduction across the 1.5B/7B pair in and out of domain; ChainPrune reports its own numbers on it directly, raising AIME24 accuracy 0.3104 to 0.3292 and AMC23 0.7016 to 0.7250 while cutting AMC23 chain length from 167 to 87 steps. As a subject of measurement, Bloom's Taxonomy profiling gives it the highest Evaluating share of the R1 distillations at 21.0% against 9.3% for the Llama-8B distillation, with Applying at 35.6%. No source reports its architecture or standalone capability figures beyond these runs.
